45:def localize(datetime: dtm.datetime, tzinfo: dtm.tzinfo) -> dtm.datetime:
46:    """Localize the datetime, both for pytz and zoneinfo timezones."""
47:    if tzinfo is UTC:
48:        return datetime.replace(tzinfo=UTC)
49:
50:    with contextlib.suppress(AttributeError):
51:        # Since pytz might not be available, we need the suppress context manager
52:        if isinstance(tzinfo, pytz.BaseTzInfo):
53:            return tzinfo.localize(datetime)
54:
55:    if datetime.tzinfo is None:
56:        return datetime.replace(tzinfo=tzinfo)
57:    return datetime.astimezone(tzinfo)

60:def to_float_timestamp(
61:    time_object: Union[float, dtm.timedelta, dtm.datetime, dtm.time],
62:    reference_timestamp: Optional[float] = None,
63:    tzinfo: Optional[dtm.tzinfo] = None,
64:) -> float:
65:    """
66:    Converts a given time object to a float POSIX timestamp.
67:    Used to convert different time specifications to a common format. The time object
68:    can be relative (i.e. indicate a time increment, or a time of day) or absolute.
69:    Objects from the :class:`datetime` module that are timezone-naive will be assumed
70:    to be in UTC, if ``bot`` is not passed or ``bot.defaults`` is :obj:`None`.
71:
72:    Args:
73:        time_object (:obj:`float` | :obj:`datetime.timedelta` | \
74:            :obj:`datetime.datetime` | :obj:`datetime.time`):
75:            Time value to convert. The semantics of this parameter will depend on its type:
76:
77:            * :obj:`float` will be interpreted as "seconds from :paramref:`reference_t`"
78:            * :obj:`datetime.timedelta` will be interpreted as
79:              "time increment from :paramref:`reference_timestamp`"
80:            * :obj:`datetime.datetime` will be interpreted as an absolute date/time value
81:            * :obj:`datetime.time` will be interpreted as a specific time of day
82:
83:        reference_timestamp (:obj:`float`, optional): POSIX timestamp that indicates the absolute
84:            time from which relative calculations are to be performed (e.g. when
85:            :paramref:`time_object` is given as an :obj:`int`, indicating "seconds from
86:            :paramref:`reference_time`"). Defaults to now (the time at which this function is
87:            called).
88:
89:            If :paramref:`time_object` is given as an absolute representation of date & time (i.e.
90:            a :obj:`datetime.datetime` object), :paramref:`reference_timestamp` is not relevant
91:            and so its value should be :obj:`None`. If this is not the case, a :exc:`ValueError`
92:            will be raised.
93:        tzinfo (:class:`datetime.tzinfo`, optional): If :paramref:`time_object` is a naive object
94:            from the :mod:`datetime` module, it will be interpreted as this timezone. Defaults to
95:            :attr:`datetime.timezone.utc` otherwise.
96:
97:            Note:
98:                Only to be used by ``telegram.ext``.
99:
100:    Returns:
101:        :obj:`float` | :obj:`None`:
102:            The return value depends on the type of argument :paramref:`time_object`.
103:            If :paramref:`time_object` is given as a time increment (i.e. as a :obj:`int`,
104:            :obj:`float` or :obj:`datetime.timedelta`), then the return value will be
105:            :paramref:`reference_timestamp` + :paramref:`time_object`.
106:
107:            Else if it is given as an absolute date/time value (i.e. a :obj:`datetime.datetime`
108:            object), the equivalent value as a POSIX timestamp will be returned.
109:
110:            Finally, if it is a time of the day without date (i.e. a :obj:`datetime.time`
111:            object), the return value is the nearest future occurrence of that time of day.
112:
113:    Raises:
114:        TypeError: If :paramref:`time_object` s type is not one of those described above.
115:        ValueError: If :paramref:`time_object` is a :obj:`datetime.datetime` and
116:            :paramref:`reference_timestamp` is not :obj:`None`.
117:    """
118:    if reference_timestamp is None:
119:        reference_timestamp = time.time()
120:    elif isinstance(time_object, dtm.datetime):
121:        raise ValueError("t is an (absolute) datetime while reference_timestamp is not None")
122:
123:    if isinstance(time_object, dtm.timedelta):
124:        return reference_timestamp + time_object.total_seconds()
125:    if isinstance(time_object, (int, float)):
126:        return reference_timestamp + time_object
127:
128:    if tzinfo is None:
129:        # We do this here rather than in the signature to ensure that we can make calls like
130:        # to_float_timestamp(
131:        #     time, tzinfo=bot.defaults.tzinfo if bot.defaults else None
132:        # )
133:        # This ensures clean separation of concerns, i.e. the default timezone should not be
134:        # the responsibility of the caller
135:        tzinfo = UTC
136:
137:    if isinstance(time_object, dtm.time):
138:        reference_dt = dtm.datetime.fromtimestamp(
139:            reference_timestamp, tz=time_object.tzinfo or tzinfo
140:        )
141:        reference_date = reference_dt.date()
142:        reference_time = reference_dt.timetz()
143:
144:        aware_datetime = dtm.datetime.combine(reference_date, time_object)
145:        if aware_datetime.tzinfo is None:
146:            # datetime.combine uses the tzinfo of `time_object`, which might be None
147:            # so we still need to localize
148:            aware_datetime = localize(aware_datetime, tzinfo)
149:
150:        # if the time of day has passed today, use tomorrow
151:        if reference_time > aware_datetime.timetz():
152:            aware_datetime += dtm.timedelta(days=1)
153:        return _datetime_to_float_timestamp(aware_datetime)
154:    if isinstance(time_object, dtm.datetime):
155:        if time_object.tzinfo is None:
156:            time_object = localize(time_object, tzinfo)
157:        return _datetime_to_float_timestamp(time_object)
158:
159:    raise TypeError(f"Unable to convert {type(time_object).__name__} object to timestamp")

168:    Wrapper over :func:`to_float_timestamp` which returns an integer (the float value truncated

170:
171:    See the documentation for :func:`to_float_timestamp` for more details.
172:    """
173:    return (
174:        int(to_float_timestamp(dt_obj, reference_timestamp, tzinfo))
175:        if dt_obj is not None
176:        else None
177:    )
178:

181:    unixtime: Optional[int],

185:    Converts an (integer) unix timestamp to a timezone aware datetime object.
186:    :obj:`None` s are left alone (i.e. ``from_timestamp(None)`` is :obj:`None`).
187:
188:    Args:
189:        unixtime (:obj:`int`): Integer POSIX timestamp.
190:        tzinfo (:obj:`datetime.tzinfo`, optional): The timezone to which the timestamp is to be
191:            converted to. Defaults to :obj:`None`, in which case the returned datetime object will
192:            be timezone aware and in UTC.
193:
194:    Returns:
195:        Timezone aware equivalent :obj:`datetime.datetime` value if :paramref:`unixtime` is not
196:        :obj:`None`; else :obj:`None`.
197:    """
198:    if unixtime is None:
199:        return None
200:"}
